decisive_items: Granulomatous inflammation with intense neutrophilic abscesses in subcutaneous fat
The hands and fingers were swollen with scattered focal purpuric infarcts
striking infiltration of the eyelids and periorbital skin with multiple firm tumorous swellings of the forehead and temples
response.rationale: R1 (erythema nodosum leprosum) best matches the acute onset, facial infiltration, purpuric infarcts, and neutrophilic abscesses on biopsy, consistent with a leprosy reaction. R4 (leprosy) is the underlying disease but lacks the specific reactional features.

rejected.why: Erythema nodosum typically presents with tender subcutaneous nodules, not facial tumorous infiltration or neutrophilic abscesses.
Relapsing polychondritis involves cartilage inflammation, absent here; no auricular or nasal cartilage findings.
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis usually has respiratory/renal involvement and necrotizing vasculitis, not this skin pattern.
Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma often has periorbital xanthomas and necrobiosis, but lacks neutrophilic abscesses and purpuric infarcts.
Leishmaniasis may have travel history but biopsy shows no parasites and clinical pattern is not typical.
Leprosy is the underlying cause but does not explain the acute reactional features such as neutrophilic abscesses and purpuric infarcts.
Granuloma annulare is usually annular papules, not diffuse infiltration with systemic symptoms and abscesses.
